title: Cost a card stand and review progress
outcomes: Cost my product and present it (links Enterprise).
Review D&T progress and add unit award evidence.
outcome:

Review D&T progress and add unit award evidence.
goal: I can explain a materials cost, present my work in my own words, and review my progress with real evidence.
success: I can show my material quantities, invented prices and total, or label an estimate.
I can explain my purpose, choices, test, change and cost in my own words.
I can check six outcome rows against real work and choose one next target.
unit_outcomes: CONSTRUCTION: design a product to solve a problem.
CONSTRUCTION: select materials and plan the build.
Cost my product and present it (links Enterprise).
Review D&T progress and add unit award evidence.
purpose: Invented client Sam needs one landscape paper prompt card, 80 mm wide by 60 mm high, kept upright and readable on a level table. The default stand has a 120 mm by 80 mm body base and fits a 160 mm by 120 mm whole table area including its channel. The card should stay for 30 seconds with hands away and be removable by hand. Review actual work against the pupil’s approved specification.
continuity: Default thin-card body 120 mm by 260 mm, folds at 80, 160 and 240 mm from one short edge; 20 mm tab inside the top seam. U channel 100 mm by 30 mm, long folds at 10 and 20 mm from one long edge; shelf out, front stop up. Paper tape cold join. Keep actual approved changes and support visible.
cost_note: These are invented classroom resource values, not supplier prices or cash spending. Charge one issued whole sheet once, including offcuts, both stand parts and the test card. Three issued 10 cm tape lengths total 30 cm and include tape offcuts. The model materials total is 45p, which is £0.45. Actual work needs its real agreed allocation, not an automatic 45p.
cost_checks: Keep planned, actual allocation and estimate separate. Name the quantity unit and invented unit price.
Charge the issued sheet once. Do not add the body, channel, test card or offcuts again. Do not recharge a retained Week 2 mock-up each week.
Record actual issued 10 cm tape portions if known. An unknown allowance is an estimate, not a measurement.
Add only a real allocated change. One extra 10 cm tape length adds 5p: 45p becomes 50p.
The model covers materials only. Labour, tools and overheads are unpriced, so this is not a full business cost.
presentation_slices: Who is the invented client? What must the stand do?
Which material and join? What did I do, and what help did I use?
What actually happened? What changed and why? Name any gap.
State my actual agreed cost or labelled estimate, with one calculation.
What have I learned? Which evidence shows it? What will I try next?
safety: Today is costing, presentation and review. No cutting or new tool work is required. Keep tools returned and the work area clear.
The adult checks a real item before handling or showing it. Do not handle damaged or suspect edges. Use a drawing or actual record if the item is not safe or available.
Present privately to an adult or use an agreed accessible mode. No forced public display, peer audience, video or personal disclosure.
Any photo is object only with no people, names or identifying background. Do not upload work or private records through the lesson page.
A printed two-minute card is a plan. Record the real observed mode, duration and help; do not invent a presentation or earlier practical evidence.
fallback: With no product, tools, paper, printer or device, hear the model prices. Use spoken sums and label your cost as an estimate. You may give a real private talk if an adult sees or hears it. Keep the actual mode, time and help. Use real work in your review, or name each gap. An adult can write your words and read them back. If no record can yet be made, the written record stays pending. Missing making, tests and actual product cost stay pending.
careers: Product makers and designers explain what a design does, what materials were used and how evidence supports a change. Enterprise work compares an asking price with all relevant costs before judging a business result.
vocabulary: How much material is issued or used, with a unit.
The invented price for one named amount, such as one sheet.
The total of the priced material allocations.
A labelled calculation based on an assumed quantity.
Real work or an observation that supports a claim.
Explaining work to an audience in an agreed form.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one cost row at a time. Pair quantity and unit price, then add subtotals. Use the five presentation prompts one at a time. Model one evidence row, then fade to a question.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept speech, signing, pointing to a prepared record or confirmed scribing. Offer a private adult audience and thinking time. Record the actual presentation mode and support, not an assumed performance.
adaptations.SEMH: Use the invented client and classroom values. No personal finances or public comparison. Let the pupil choose private feedback and an agreed calm pause. Gaps lead to a next step, not public judgement.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Provide a large cost table, read-aloud values and adult handling of an approved object. No tool use is required. Use a safe drawing or record when touching or showing an item is unsuitable.
adaptations.Literacy and Numeracy: Keep pence beside each value. Multiply quantities by the price for that unit, then add. Model 45p equals£0.45. Provide short presentation sentence starts and read each scribed statement back.
adaptations.EAL: Rehearse in any language. Pair quantity, price and total with the model row. Preserve the pupil meaning in own-word presentation or confirmed scribing. Do not mistake language support for missing understanding.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Gather the real record
pupil: Find your design, plan, build and test records.
Use actual work or mark a gap.
Today we cost, present and review the whole unit.
stages.teacher: Retrieve the actual design, cutting list, model or product, change log and Week 4 evaluation. Read both exact weekly outcomes from the plan. Narrative calls the award only the unit award. Missing work is marked missing; an adult model may support a labelled estimate but never replaces a pupil record. Offer a calm settling pause inside the stage.
stages.check: Ask for one real record and one thing it shows. If absent, identify the gap and a next opportunity; do not invent earlier success.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: What are we pricing
pupil: Use invented classroom values, not shop prices.
One sheet costs 30p. One 10 cm tape length costs 5p.
Cost the agreed allocation once.
stages.teacher: Explain material allocation with the model sheet. A 210 by 297 mm sheet holds the 120 by 260 mm body, rotated 30 by 100 mm channel and 80 by 60 mm test card in its remaining 90 mm strip. The whole sheet includes offcuts. Retained mock-up or test card is not charged again each week. Actual different material uses a recorded adult-agreed value; unknown quantity is an estimate.
stages.check: Ask whether the test card needs a second charge after pricing its whole issued sheet. No. Model values are not supplier quotes or actual spending.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: Show the materials cost
pupil: Watch quantity times unit price.
One sheet: 1 × 30p = 30p.
Three tape lengths: 3 × 5p = 15p.
stages.teacher: Model the two cost rows with quantities and units. The 30 cm tape model is an issued allowance including offcuts, not a claim that a pupil measured 30 cm. State 45p materials cost only. Labour, tools and overheads are unpriced. With a 60p budget, 15p remains; that is different from any selling margin. Fade the worked total and ask the group to complete a changed quantity.
stages.check: Ask how many 10 cm tape lengths make 30 cm. Three. Check the pupil uses 5p per length, not 5p per cm. Reteach the unit before adding.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Cost a real change and plan the talk
pupil: One extra 10 cm tape length adds 5p.
The model total changes from 45p to 50p.
Use the two-minute card to plan your own words.
stages.teacher: Compare the model with an actual agreed allocation. Add an extra tape portion only if actually issued or clearly label a hypothetical comparison. Optional finishing paper is 5p only if allocated; it is not in the default total. Model a short own-word presentation using five timed prompts that total 120 seconds. Keep actual test findings, changes and help explicit. No public audience is required.
stages.check: Ask which cost changed and why. Then ask the pupil to link one presentation claim to a real record or clearly label a model estimate.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: Check for double counting
pupil: The whole sheet already cost 30p.
Should you add the test card price again?
Choose add again, do not add again, or guess.
stages.teacher: Hinge answer: do not add again. The issued whole sheet includes both parts, the test card and offcuts. If anyone double counts, point to the one sheet and cross out the duplicate model line. Parallel check: an invented asking price is 90p and materials cost 45p. Is 45p the final net profit? No; it is above materials cost before unpriced labour, tools and overheads. Recheck with a fresh explanation.
stages.check: Move on when the pupil prices the allocation once and distinguishes materials cost from full business cost. Otherwise use Supported with the two model rows and a labelled estimate.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: My cost talk and progress review
pupil: Complete your cost sheet or labelled estimate.
Present in your own words using an agreed mode.
Check six outcome rows against real evidence.
Keep one gap and one next target visible.
stages.teacher: Use one route. Pupils prepare briefly, then use the two-minute card within these eight minutes. For a small group, private adult presentations can run in a short rota while others cost and review; use an agreed paired or other accessible mode only with genuine observation and pupil consent. Do not force an audience or add time beyond the lesson. If everyone cannot be observed, record actual presentations only and keep remaining ones pending. Review the grid from real records; a tick is lesson evidence, not award completion.
stages.check: Check quantity, unit, price, total and estimate label; observe actual presentation mode/duration/support where it happens. For each grid status ask for a date, location and comment. Preserve pupil own words.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Check the evidence and the claim
pupil: Read your total and explain one calculation.
Confirm what you really presented and what is still pending.
Choose one future target from the grid.
stages.teacher: Offer a private review. Correct any duplicate material charge or pence conversion. Confirm actual presentation record, duration, support and evidence location. If a cost or presentation is incomplete, retain that status. Review five weeks with six outcomes because Week 5 has two. Let the pupil correct scribed words. Tidy safe items inside the final minute.
stages.check: Pupil explains one cost or labelled estimate, one real progress claim and one next target. A printed presentation card alone does not prove presenting.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My progress and next step
pupil: My materials cost or estimate is ___ because ___.
One real record shows I can ___.
My next target is ___.
stages.teacher: Retain the pupil cost sheet, presentation record, progress reflection and closing grid. Mark missing evidence and actual support. No certification or whole-award completion is inferred. Use the final minute to confirm the pupil meaning and return safe items.
stages.check: The evidence records actual costing, presenting and review separately. An estimate, planned talk and completed presentation must not be confused.

Supported: Use the two model cost rows with an adult. Say whether they match your real allocation or are an estimate.
Multiply 1 sheet by 30p and 3 tape lengths by 5p, then add once.
Use five short spoken prompts for a private or accessible presentation. Record what really happened.
Review each outcome with a real record, support and one next target.
Standard: Use your actual adult-agreed material allocation or clearly label an estimate.
Show quantity, unit price, subtotal, total and a real cost change.
Plan and give an own-word two-minute presentation in an agreed mode.
Check all six outcome rows across five weeks. Name a real strength, gap and next target.
Stretch: Finish your own cost, talk record and progress review first.
Compare your plan with what was really issued. Count any waste once.
Use a made-up asking price of 90p. Find the amount above materials cost.
Say why that is not net profit. Choose a next step from a real gap.
